narrative:
Friday is literally “the calm before the storm” -- mostly cloudy but dry and pleasant. Clouds thicken tonight, and showers develop from southwest to northeast late tonight.

The story is Isaias. It is a Category 2 hurricane south of Alabama and Mississippi today, barreling toward landfall near the Alabama-Florida line this evening. The forecast track has shifted slightly right into Middle Tennessee and then east-northeast. That small shift raises the ante somewhat for us. Saturday is cool and rainy with rain increasing late in the day. The problem remains inflow bands from the Atlantic Saturday night and early Sunday. The good news is a faster exit. Rain tapers to showers by noon Sunday with showers lingering into early Monday, mostly on the west side of the Appalachians. Windy conditions continue through Monday. It's not Helene, but it is a significant storm nonetheless.

Bottom lines:

Total rain in NW NC will be between 3 and 5 inches for most of the eastern half of the region (maybe less in Ashe and Alleghany counties) with lesser amounts toward the NC/TN border.
Winds become gusty beginning Saturday night. Higher elevations can expect gusts to 55 mph; valleys will have gusts closer to 40 mph.

Impacts: Stream flooding is likely, mostly in the eastern half of the region. With leaves still on the trees, a few trees will probably fall. Secure your property, or you may be sharing your deck furniture with your neighbors.

Forecast Discussion

I will not repeat all the information from the long Introduction, but I will add some detail.

A front moved through yesterday with little noticeable impact. We have more clouds today, and temperatures are a couple degrees cooler.

This forecast is not a major change but is “one tick up” on the intensity measures for rain and wind because of the slightly more easterly track of the storm. It also includes a faster exit.

I’ll share a total precip map, but DO NOT TAKE THIS LITERALLY. I cannot find a model output that I’m totally happy with. I think rain will be a bit heavier near the Blue Ridge than shown here, and Saturday night is tricky with the feeder bands in play. So the map is decent overall, but there will be locally higher amounts.

Here’s a wind gust forecast map. The numbers you see are for the towns below them. Expect 50+ mph gusts at higher elevations.

A front associated with the remnant low from Isaias will move through early Sunday morning and sweep the heaviest precipitation to our east. Then NW flow showers develop, affecting mostly the western half of the Appalachians. These showers end early Monday morning.

High pressure will build in from our southwest Monday and Tuesday. Winds will gradually settle, and we will be back to pleasant weather Tuesday.

A weak front moves through Wednesday with a “barely worth mentioning” afternoon shower.

Pleasant October weather remains with us Thursday and Friday as high pressure moves into the Mid-Atlantic.
